findings.text: follow-on: a request skipped because a live follower this host did not start holds the pair is never recorded in self._children, so tick() never revisits it; when that follower later exits, the host does not take over and the session is left unwatched.
follow-on: no test drives the `crew host` CLI verb or its --fd/--fifo/--owner-pid options; the gate runs `python -m reckon.crew.session_host` directly, so the added CLI plumbing is unverified.

follow-on: the owner-identity environment name and JSON encoding are duplicated here and inline at session_host.py:343, rather than reusing reckon/crew/runs.py:2873 and reckon/crew/runs.py:2917 which own that encoding.
follow-on: the child-stderr filename is `<pid>-<start>.json.log` (the record stem plus .log), not the `<claude-pid>-<start>.log` path the plan section names.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 0dbf9865; two commits, four files, +1183/-13, every changed file inside the declared write scope and every line the node's own authorship.
item_verdicts.done_when: the section's done-when names five observable facts; tests/test_session_host.py asserts each (one child per pair at :291, a killed child restarted at :316, a hand-armed live follower left alone at :331, no host stdout at :348, no child surviving the host's SIGTERM at :361 or its owner's exit at :378), and my re-run of the gate reads 9 passed EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is the section-4 deliverable, a hidden `reckon crew host` that supervises one `crew follow` per project and session for one Claude session; reckon/crew/session_host.py:210 SessionHost implements it and reckon/cli.py:4743 exposes the verb.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits 87cc79c61 and 241b80161, changed_paths and commits populated, negative_control_log names a log whose last line is EXIT=1 with one failing id the head arm does not fail; baseline_suite/after_suite are absent, so the added-failure count is unmeasured rather than zero.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared paths; the diff is four files, all inside them (reckon/crew/session_host.py, reckon/cli.py, tests/test_session_host.py, the evidence fragment); the declared figures directory docs/figures/a-follower-lives-as-long-as-its-session/session-host-supervises-followers was not emitted.

justifications.durability: the declared negative control (no parent-death signal, owner-liveness stop removed) reddens exactly tests/test_session_host.py:378 test_no_child_survives_its_owners_exit at 1 failed EXIT=1, so the teardown guard is falsified; the other assertions read independent process facts (a follower-written marker, /proc liveness, the host's stdout) rather than a value the test handed in.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_session_host.py asserts all five done-when clauses as 9 passed EXIT=0, but the roughly eighty lines added at reckon/cli.py:4743 (the `crew host` verb and its --fd/--fifo plumbing) are reached by no test, because the gate drives the module directly with `python -m reckon.crew.session_host`.
justifications.fit: session_host.py follows the surrounding crew idiom (a dataclass, a hidden CLI verb with lazy imports, a mechanism docstring) and carries no plan, version or ticket label on any added line.
justifications.goal_fidelity: session_host.py:210 runs one crew follow per (project, session) with stdout inherited and stderr to a log, restarts a dead child through fleet_supervisor.next_backoff, and stops every child on owner end or signal, which is the section's deliverable.
justifications.reuse: the restart schedule reuses fleet_supervisor.next_backoff, but the owner-identity mechanism is re-declared at session_host.py:79 and :343 instead of extending its owner reckon/crew/runs.py:2873 _FOLLOWER_OWNER_ENV and runs.py:2917 _format_follower_owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: the four changed files are all inside the declared write paths, and the only departure is the declared docs/figures/... directory left unemitted, which is under-delivery rather than an out-of-scope write.
